paymentMethods.cashAdvice: Check the business's displayed payment options before ordering; merchants choose which card brands and types they accept.

culturalTips: Restaurant service is included in the bill; Portugal's tourism board describes an additional tip of roughly 5–10% as customary.

paymentMethods.cashAdvice: Card payments are common in towns and tourist areas. Poland uses złoty rather than the euro; check your card issuer's overseas charges.
Keep yen available as a backup: some small businesses accept cash only, and an overseas card may not work at every terminal.

culturalTips: Tipping is generally not expected in restaurants, taxis and hotels. Some private guides or interpreters accustomed to overseas visitors may accept a discreet gratuity.

paymentMethods.cashAdvice: Cash, debit cards and credit cards are common payment options. Confirm acceptance in advance; Switzerland's national currency is the Swiss franc.

culturalTips: A tip is optional in Switzerland; guests are not obliged to leave one.

paymentMethods.cashAdvice: Argentina's tourism board reports that credit cards are accepted by many businesses. Confirm your specific card with each venue; this guide does not quote exchange rates or card conversion benefits.
Check displayed payment methods and any minimum card amount before ordering. Businesses may decline card payments; carry an alternative way to pay.
